Problem: Joe was in charge of lights for a dance. The red light blinks every two seconds, the yellow light every three seconds, and the blue light every five seconds. If we include the very beginning and very end of the dance, how many times during a seven minute dance will all the lights come on at the same time? (Assume that all three lights blink simultaneously at the very beginning of the dance.)

Solve step by step. End with: The answer is [your answer].

message.content:
The red light blinks every 2 seconds, the yellow every 3 seconds, and the blue every 5 seconds.

All three lights come on together at times that are common multiples of 2, 3, and 5.

\[
\text{LCM}(2,3,5)=30
\]

So all three lights blink together every 30 seconds.

A seven-minute dance is:

\[
7 \times 60 = 420 \text{ seconds}
\]

We include the beginning at \(0\) seconds and the end at \(420\) seconds. The simultaneous blink times are:

\[
0, 30, 60, 90, \dots, 420
\]

This is counting multiples of 30 from 0 to 420 inclusive:

\[
\frac{420}{30}+1 = 14+1 = 15
\]

So all three lights come on at the same time 15 times.

The answer is 15.
